subject: Request: Temporary SLA exception for content-filter & tool-call failures
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@clarionsys.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@clarionsys.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 13:14:00 +0000
Subject: Clarion SLA request: filter/tool-call structured-output exceptions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before Procurement signs, our security and compliance team flagged a potential issue around content filtering and downstream tool-calling failures. Clarion performs regulated document ingest where we must guarantee redaction and deterministic structured output for certain fields.

Two asks from our side:
- We need a defined operational posture when Redwood's content filters or tool-calling produce failures that either (a) block expected structured outputs or (b) increase latency beyond our agreed P50/P95.
- Procurement would prefer an explicit carve-type exception in the SLA that allows temporary deviations for these filter/tool-related incidents while we iterate on prompt+schema alignment, but we need objective thresholds and reporting so it isn't open-ended.

I attached the redlines our legal team suggested (clarion-sla-redlines_20260812.pdf) and a short log sample of a recent failure case (filter-failure-logs.zip). Can your team sketch acceptable guardrails (detection metrics, maximum exception window, rollback/fallback behavior, and proposed commercial remedies)?

Appreciate it — Elena
Senior Director, Product Security
Clarion Systems

----
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@clarionsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurements@clarionsys.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarion SLA request: filter/tool-call structured-output exceptions

Elena — thanks for the detailed note and the attachments, which I shared with our reliability and legal teams. High level proposal from Redwood to keep this short and actionable:

Proposed guardrails (draft):
- Scope: only for "filter-triggered blocking" and "tool-call structured-output failures" as evidenced by error logs and our tracing (we’ll require the sample you included for each incident).
- Detection metrics: filter_fallback_rate (percent of requests that hit filter-caused fallback), tool_call_error_rate, median_inference_latency (ms), and 95th percentile latency (ms).
- Exception window: initial exceptions allowed up to 14 days per incident, with automatic rollback to safe-mode after 72 hours if remediation progress is insufficient.
- Reporting: weekly incident report during the exception window with raw traces and redaction-safe artifacts.
- Commercial: for exceptions >72 hours we propose a pro-rated credit at 5% of monthly invoice for each additional 7-day block (capped at 25% for that month).

Next steps: if Clarion agrees in principle we’ll have Rishi draft the technical detection thresholds and Marissa will propose the commercial clause to be inserted into the SLA amendment. Legal can then turn that into a DocuSign attachment.

Can you confirm Clarion can accept the 14-day max initial window and the reporting cadence? If not, tell us what you'd prefer and we’ll iterate.

—Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

----
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@clarionsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarion SLA request: filter/tool-call structured-output exceptions

Quick technical note on what we can commit to and how we detect:

Detection approach:
- filter_fallback_rate: We define a fallback when the filter pipeline returns a non-actionable token mask that prevents schema extraction or when the model chooses to refuse output due to content rules. We can detect this via a filter flag in the response envelope (existing runtime field).
- tool_call_error_rate: Any non-200 from a tool call or a tool response that fails schema validation counts.
- latency bloom: track P50/P95 per-route; we can tag incidents where P95 exceeds baseline + 250ms for >=10% of requests over a 15-minute rolling window.

Operational mitigations we can implement during an exception window:
- Transparent degraded mode: return a structured fallback payload with an explicit "filter_degraded":true flag so Clarion's downstream systems can safely skip automated downstream processing.
- Conditional routing: route to a compatibility model variant without the strict filter layer (customer opt-in) — this reduces false positives but slightly increases residual risk; can be timeboxed by exception window.
- Rate-limited retries and queueing to avoid cascading latency spikes.

Monitoring and evidence:
- We will provide a weekly package with redaction-safe traces, counts, and example payloads; production-level P95/P99 histograms; and the exact runtime flags that caused fallback.

Caveats:
- If Clarion requires absolute deterministic redaction at all times, that is not compatible with our hosted runtime guarantees without more restrictive model variants and additional validation layers; that would push to a Private deployment or Dedicated pool.

I’ll attach a short spec of the runtime flags and threshold values in the follow-up if this approach is acceptable.

—Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@clarionsys.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@clarionsys.com, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 08:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarion SLA request: filter/tool-call structured-output exceptions

Elena — glad to see a pragmatic path forward. From a commercial perspective we can offer the following amendment language to insert into the SOW: 

- Exception duration: up to 14 calendar days per incident; automatically reviewed at day 7 with joint remediation plan.
- Fallback disclosure: Redwood will flag affected responses with a runtime header and include a weekly report.
- Credits: If an exception extends beyond 72 hours, a single 7-day extension will be granted at no charge; subsequent extensions (per 7-day block) will incur a credit equal to 5% of monthly service fees, capped at 25% for that billing month.

If Clarion prefers firm uptime guarantees instead of credits, we can discuss Dedicated capacity or Private deployment pricing that supports stricter redaction SLAs. Also tagging Karthik from Legal to coordinate the exact redline language.

If this is acceptable, we’ll prepare the DocuSign amendment and route to Procurement.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior AE, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@clarionsys.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@clarionsys.com, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2026 15:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarion SLA request: filter/tool-call structured-output exceptions

Thanks — this is helpful. Clarion accepts the 14-day initial window and the 72-hour escalation threshold, conditional on:

- Weekly reports including the runtime flags and one redaction-safe example per incident.
- A clear rollback/compatibility path (we prefer the routing to a compatibility model variant but would like the option to schedule a short freeze on automated downstream publishing during remediation).

Procurement will expect the DocuSign amendment (please include the credit language and the reporting cadence). Once we have the DocuSign we’ll start a 30-day pilot with the exception clause active. I’ve CC’d procurement.

Elena
Senior Director, Product Security
Clarion Systems

Attachments referenced: clarion-sla-redlines_20260812.pdf, filter-failure-logs.zip
